narrative.overview:
A terminal left running on a Tokyo side street, kept by one person who built everything on it. The page is a near-black room with a faint 120px grid on the wall and violet light falling from the header. Two neon colours do all the talking: cyan where something can be done, magenta where something is being named or answered. Everything else is ink, grey and hairline.

Density is unhurried. Type is large, sections sit far apart, and the personal projects carry the most mass on the page. Ornament is line-work drawn at low opacity: the asanoha hemp-leaf lattice, the seigaiha wave horizon and the scanlines over images. Each should register only when you look for it. The world's humour lives in monospaced marginalia that read like telephony and DOS output, set small and grey beside the real content.

The system rejects corporate templates and loud cyberpunk: heavy glitch, flicker, chromatic aberration. It also rejects retro-web costume and Japanese characters used as decoration; the Japanese reference is carried by geometry alone.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground with a fixed 120px hairline grid and one violet glow from the top of the page.
Two neon accents with separate jobs: cyan acts, magenta names and answers hover.
Onest for everything read; Roboto Mono for everything logged.
Line-only traditional patterns, faded by mask, never filled with colour.
Flat at rest; depth appears only as a response to a pointer.
Motion on arrival and on state change only. Nothing loops.

rules.name: The Two Tubes Rule
rules.body: Every action is cyan at rest and no action is magenta at rest. Magenta names the person and answers the pointer: a hover on a cyan text link or a neutral link goes to magenta. Both tubes may also light the world's line-work and CRT sketches.

rules.name: The Spill Rule
rules.body: Violet is light, not paint. It appears as the header's radial glow and never as a fill, a border or a text colour; only its pale tint may colour text, and only on a timeline chip.

rules.name: The Brand Marks Rule
rules.body: Skill chips may carry a technology's own colour, mixed toward white for the icon (72%) and toward Hairline for the border (45%). No other component borrows outside colour.

rules.name: The Logged Voice Rule
rules.body: Mono is reserved for what a machine would print: dates, paths, signals, commands, field labels, a project's technology row. Sentences a person says stay in Onest.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Mono labels keep their source case with no added tracking. Capitals appear only where the machine would print them: INVITE, ACK, BYE, a DOS path, the text of a CRT screen.

rules.name: The Call Sequence Rule
rules.body: Page order follows the call. INVITE opens the hero, section signals advance through 100 Trying, 180 Ringing, 200 OK and ACK, and BYE closes the footer. A new section takes its place in the sequence with a real SIP message.

rules.name: The Almost-Imperceptible Rule
rules.body: Atmosphere stays at the opacities the build set: grid at 3.5% white, scanlines at 20% void every 3px, asanoha at 42%, seigaiha at 32%. If an effect is the first thing you notice, it is too strong.

rules.name: The Still Light Rule
rules.body: Light never moves. Scanlines, glows and the cursor are static; they do not animate, pulse or blink.

dos: Do make every action cyan at rest and move hovers to magenta, except filled buttons, which lift to Lit Cyan.
Do give every new section a real SIP signal in its heading, in sequence.
Do set dates, paths and signals in Roboto Mono at 14px or 12px.
Do gate lift and scale behind a real pointer, and remove every transform under reduced motion.
Do keep the name and all revealed content fully visible when animation does not run.
Do use the 2px cyan outline at 3px offset for every keyboard focus state.
Do swap a CRT screen for a real screenshot in the same scanlined frame as soon as one exists.
donts: Don't add heavy glitch, flicker or chromatic aberration; scanlines, glow and the cursor stay static and faint.
Don't use Japanese characters as decoration; asanoha and seigaiha carry the reference as line-work.
Don't extend the DOS path or `C:\>` line into windows, title bars, taskbars, boot screens or other operating-system costume, or into GeoCities-style retro-web pastiche.
Don't fill the asanoha or seigaiha with colour, or raise them above the opacities in the Almost-Imperceptible Rule.
Don't add a resting neon glow to any element.
Don't add looping animation, including a blinking cursor.
Don't give another section the visual weight of the project cards.
Don't show an invented fact on a surface; missing data is hidden.
